title: LLM KPI summarizer + ephemeral metric allocator for high-cardinality inference signals
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Our current metrics ingestion path struggles with transient high-cardinality inference signals (model:variant:prompt_hash:user_tier combinations) which causes Prometheus scraping pressure, sticky series explosion in long-tail workloads, and expensive retention costs. Goal: implement a lightweight 'multiplexing summarizer' and an ephemeral metric allocator that reduces cardinality for Prometheus while preserving SLO-relevant fidelity for latency/error KPIs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) OTel->inbound-proxy accepts enriched inference spans and routes to summarizer. 2) Summarizer emits stable low-cardinality Prometheus metrics (histogram + aggregated labels) while forwarding full granular events to long-term storage (OTLP/Clickhouse) for debugging. 3) Latency SLOs computed from summarized streams differ from full-resolution SLO by <= 2% on test workloads. 4) End-to-end added cost <= 10% of current ingestion baseline (measured in prod-canary).
implementation_notes: Architecture: deploy a horizontally scalable summarizer service in the telemetry tier. It maintains ephemeral allocation tables keyed by (model, model_version, route_bucket) with TTL-based decay. For heavy keys, we emit aggregated histogram slices and a sampling factor label. For rare keys, we keep a 'sticky micro-bucket' count for hotspot detection and forward raw events asynchronously to the event lake. Use OTLP transform hook to attach sampling_factor and allocator_id. Prometheus exporter converts summarized histograms to Prometheus histograms with fixed buckets to stabilize cardinality. Trade-offs: this increases complexity in pipeline and adds asynchronous storage dependency but avoids 10-100x time-series growth. Memory: ephemeral allocator uses LRU with soft-eviction and backpressure to prevent OOM.
design_decisions: Use TTL decay (default 2 hours) to let ephemeral allocators age out vs manual eviction policy to avoid manual tuning
Emit a sampling_factor label instead of per-user_id labels to keep cardinality bounded
Keep a configurable 'debug-forward' percentage (default 0.5%) of raw events to Clickhouse for incident postmortem
Prometheus exporter uses fixed 10 histogram buckets chosen to match observed token-latency distribution; decision made after benchmarking dataset A/B runs
risks_mitigations: Risk: mis-estimation of sampling_factor could bias SLOs. Mitigation: run canary comparing summarized SLO vs raw SLO over 7d and auto-correct sampling rules
Risk: increased end-to-end pipeline latency. Mitigation: make summarizer async for tail-case forwarding and enforce 200ms processing SLO with shedding when overloaded
Risk: data-loss of rare events. Mitigation: always forward a small debug sample to long-term store and surface alerts for allocator saturation
